messages:
Eli: late-night experiment — looking for a short weird novel (sub-200p) and a gritty cassette/synth playlist to read it to. cozy-but-uneasy vibes.
Rachel: try 'The Comforters' by Muriel Spark (short, uncanny). pairs with early 80s analog synth.
Vince: playlist rec: "Neon Tape Mess" (I made it, lots of tape-hiss textures). link: https://open.spotify.example/neontape (not real)
Marisol: 'The Comforters' is perfect. also consider 'The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle' excerpts if you don't mind serialized reading.
Olivia: if you want micro-fiction, 'In Watermelon Sugar' is trippy and compact. read with minimal, reverb-drenched synths.
Eli: love these. anyone got a short visual — like a 30–60 min film/TV short — to watch between chapters?
Vince: watch 'La Jetee' (1962) if you haven't. photo-essay film, very tape-era melancholy.
Rachel: yes to La Jetee. also archive.org has weird 70s arts shorts (grainy mono) that set the mood.
Marisol: poll-bot: POLL CREATED by Eli — "Which pairing should I try first?" — options: 1) Comforters + Neon Tape Mess, 2) Wind-Up Excerpt + La Jetee, 3) In Watermelon Sugar + 70s arts shorts — ends in 3h
Olivia: voted 3. tiny book + grainy film sounds divine.
Vince: voted 1. (I will also share the playlist after lunch)
Rachel: voted 2. fine art sadness.
Eli: voted 3. thanks everyone, I'll do a listening+reading session Fri night and post a pic of the setup. bonus if anyone has cassette shops or cheap deck recs.
Marisol: cassette shop shout: 'Loop & Spool' in Portland has reissues and friendly staff.
Vince: if you need a low-cost deck, check thrift or the crosley used-market, but avoid belt issues — test playback.
Olivia: tip: a phone running a tiny wow&flutter app + headphone amp can fake cassette warble if you don't have tapes.
Eli: perfect. i'll report back with pictures and a short micro-review. goodnight folks :crescent_moon:
